Anthropic released Claude 4 as two distinct models, Opus 4 and Sonnet 4, on May 8, 2025 [Source: ev-1]. The launch signaled that the agentic-coding market was entering a phase defined by reliability and enterprise adoption rather than just raw capability. Specifically, Anthropic positioned the Claude 4 family as the "safest and most reliable coding agent," with its headline feature being "computer use 2.0" (browser control) which was roughly twice as reliable as the previous generation's capabilities [Source: ev-1].

The dual-model strategy allowed Anthropic to target different segments of this market:
*   **Opus 4** served as the flagship model ("Claude 4") priced at $15 per million input tokens and $75 per million output tokens [Source: ev-1].
*   **Sonnet 4** acted as a fast workhorse, priced lower at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, positioning it specifically as the developer-default coding model [Source: ev-1].

This launch was timed to coincide with the rise of Claude Code, which became the defining agentic-coding product of 2025, amidst an "enterprise agentic-coding gold rush" driven by competition from OpenAI's o-series [Source: ev-1]. The market signal was further reinforced when Anthropic reported record API usage and subsequently raised a large funding round in late September 2025 at a valuation of approximately $183 billion, cementing its position as the leader in this sector [Source: ev-1].
